svg.title: The release path as it runs: eight authorization stages from LOCK to FIRE, the guard registry above, the pipeline activation key below, the external candidate lane feeding in, the unbuilt promotion lane, and the four live defects at the exact points they sit.
svg.text: The release path as it runs
Eight stages declared as data in vault/tools/lib/release_bindings.py:93 (MACRO_SEQUENCE): each names the evidence store that answers “did this happen” and the module that owns its reader.
MACRO_SEQUENCE declares no step order of its own; the runner (tropo-release-run.py, 1,196 lines, execute=False by default) stays the authority on micro-order.
FIRE is the one stage whose gate is authorization plus completion rather than mere occurrence. Every path, line number and count below re-verified at HEAD b7555b5b5 on 2026-09-08.

Ratchets missed and disclosed, not softened: 33h 22m
four fire pastes against 1, each stopped by a defect.
.tropo/scripts/lib/release_authorization.py — refuses a build or a public
upload without a runtime-minted fingerprint proving a real pipeline run
occurred. Tamper-evidence, not cryptography — the module says so in its
engine-stamped actor, requires a registered principal, and excludes
anyone who executed a step in the run — but nothing is signed. The
un-forgeable control is the outward act.
called at four points on the path ↑

3 · The fire selects its artifact by mtime
sp.stat().st_mtime and returns the newest. It is the
default resolution at three call sites (:2730, :2745,
:3159). Nothing refuses a stage belonging to a different
release — the release tool never tells the publisher
which run is firing, so every downstream check reads its
facts out of the same selected record and they agree by
construction. All of it is live at HEAD.
Mike held the cure on 2026-09-07 and released the hold
at 23:51Z ("I choose 1"): the function is deleted rather
than repaired, inside the promotion-lane spec below.
4 · Skipped gates print green at the fire
tallies only refused and errored outcomes. A gate that
reported skipped-inputs-absent — one that never ran —
falls through to "PREFLIGHT GREEN — {n} gate(s) passed;
the fire cannot refuse on a precondition." The shape
underneath is one line: release_gates.py:262 counts
VERDICT_SKIPPED as ok. The candidate phase treats
skipped as a refusal for exactly this reason; the
Open at HEAD; the tally fix is routed to Argus as a task
The promotion lane — RULED, SPEC LOCKED, UNBUILT (dashed: does not exist yet)
ls vault/tools | grep -i promot → empty. The design-spec f015ee0c7ea5 is status: locked (Mike, 2026-09-07), assigned to Argus, target_release 1.96.0.
About +230 lines including tests, two files shrinking, zero new tools, one `promote` subcommand — and _latest_staged_version() deleted rather than guarded.

What it converts is the four fire pastes: shipping becomes promotion of a candidate already built and already green, not a founder-triggered construction that decides at the outward edge whether construction succeeded.

Its two constraints, from the released hold note f0154d94f0ea — C1: a fire refuses when the record it selected is already published. C2: the artifact is bound by name to the run shipping it, never inferred from disk recency.
The apparatus it would allow deleting measures 3,513 lines at HEAD (tropo-release.py, release_authorization.py, release_saga.py, release_legs.py, tropo-freeze-release-candidate.py).
PROVEN — has run against the world and could have failed
BUILT BUT UNPROVEN, ruled-and-unbuilt, or deliberately held
KNOWN BROKEN — a live defect at HEAD
